Not every stream answered at the new address. Save anyway if the camera is not reachable yet, for example because it still has to move.
Frigate restarts to use the new address; live view and recording stop for a moment.
Most cameras answer on port 80; some on 8000 or 8899. ONVIF has to be on in the camera.
Frigate is connecting to the camera and opening its streams; this takes up to half a minute.
Tick the streams to use: usually the main stream for recording and the sub stream for detection.
Tick at least one stream that works.
Detection takes one stream, recording one, audio one. Through go2rtc the camera is opened once and shared, which most cameras like better.
Recordings in h265 play on iPhone, iPad and Mac only with this on.
Frigate starts the camera at once; no restart needed. The camera\'s password is kept in Frigate\'s config, as with Frigate\'s own wizard.
Detection uses a large stream; a sub stream takes far less of the server.
The detection stream is very small; objects will be hard to see.
Recordings will have no sound: the stream has no audio.
The audio is not AAC; recordings may play without sound in some players.

Drag a corner to move it. Tap + between two corners to add one; long-press a corner to remove it.
None selected: every tracked object counts.

An object must be in the zone this many frames in a row before it counts; a few avoids short false entries. Loitering: an object that stays longer is marked as loitering (0 is off).
